formula_archetype: A3B2

discriminate_from.nias: the Al3Ni2 type is the ordered-vacancy derivative of the NiAs B8_1 / Ni2In B8_2 pair: one third of the metal sites of the filled Ni2In variant are empty and the vacancies order into alternate layers, which lowers the symmetry from P6_3/mmc (194) to P-3m1 (164) and fixes the composition at A3B2 rather than leaving it a variable interstitial range
discriminate_from.alb2: also trigonal with a small hexagonal cell, but AlB2 has a planar graphite-like B net and full occupancy, not ordered metal vacancies
discriminate_from.laves_phase: not a tetrahedrally close-packed AB2 structure
discriminate_from.cdi2_1t: the anion-layer analogue is coincidental; Al3Ni2 is a metallic 3D framework, not a van der Waals layered compound

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 019: six of the seven samples of the In-Ni host are In3Ni2, and Materials Project gives In3Ni2 P-3m1 (164) mp-21385 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references. The taxonomy carries nias but has no entry for its ordered-vacancy A3B2 derivative, so the host could not be labelled without one.
The same structure type covers a sizeable group of group-10/group-13 intermetallics (Ni2In3, Ni2Ga3, Ni2Al3, Pd3Bi2), so the entry is likely to be reused rather than being a single-host convenience.
mp_id is left null here per the taxonomy policy; mp-21385 is cited as the evidence that the structure is real, not filled in as the prototype structure.

formula_archetype: A(x)NbO2 with 0.5 < x <= 1

discriminate_from.naxcoo2_layered: the closest relative and the one it is most likely to be confused with. In gamma-NaxCoO2 the transition metal is octahedrally coordinated and the alkali sits in trigonal-prismatic interlayer sites; LiNbO2 is the inverse -- niobium is trigonal-prismatically coordinated inside the layer and lithium takes octahedral interlayer sites. Both are P6_3/mmc, so the space group does not separate them and the coordination has to be checked
discriminate_from.alpha_nafeo2_layered: R-3m with octahedral transition metal and octahedral alkali; a different stacking and a different symmetry
discriminate_from.perovskite: LiNbO3 is the perovskite-related ferroelectric of the same binary and is a different compound entirely -- the O:Nb ratio is 3 rather than 2
discriminate_from.mos2_2h: the same trigonal-prismatic coordination and the same space group, but MoS2 layers are held by van der Waals contact with nothing between them, whereas LiNbO2 has an ionically bound alkali layer that is the doping variable

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 019: all six compositions of the Li-Nb-O host are Li(x)NbO2 with x = 0.6 to 1.0, and Materials Project gives LiNbO2 P6_3/mmc (194) mp-3924 at hull 0.000 with 6 ICSD references. The taxonomy had only LiNbO3 chemistry available (perovskite-adjacent), which is the wrong compound.

The lithium content is a compositional variable, not a dopant: Li is deintercalated down to about x = 0.5 and carries the material from a band insulator into a metal, and superconductivity near 5 K is reported in the deintercalated range. Stage 3 should treat x the way it treats x in NaxCoO2 rather than as a doping level.

Niobium sits in trigonal prisms of oxygen, which is unusual for an early transition metal oxide and is the structural reason for the narrow d band that makes the compound interesting thermoelectrically.

formula_archetype: MX2 (M = group 5-6 transition metal, X mainly Te)
typical_space_group: P2_1/m (11) for 1T-prime; Pmn2_1 (31) for the polar Td variant; C2/m (12) for NbTe2 and TaTe2

discriminate_from.mos2_2h: 2H has undistorted trigonal-prismatic coordination and a real band gap; 1T-prime is octahedral with the metal atoms displaced into zigzag metal-metal chains, which closes the gap and makes it a semimetal. In the Mo-Te chemistry the two are polymorphs of one compound with very different transport, so the distinction is the whole point
discriminate_from.cdi2_1t: the undistorted octahedral 1T parent. 1T-prime is its Peierls-distorted derivative -- same layer topology, lower symmetry, metal-metal bonded chains. Use cdi2_1t only when the octahedral layer is genuinely undistorted
discriminate_from.nbse3_chain: a true chain compound built of trigonal-prismatic MX3 columns, not a distorted layer
discriminate_from.misfit_layered_chalcogenide: single-component layers, not two interleaved incommensurate subsystems

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 019 (Mo-Nb-Te). The gap was already recorded in chunk 007: the Mo-Te record put beta/1T-prime MoTe2 (P2_1/m, mp-7459) into other_polymorphs as unresolved_crystalline with the explicit note that the taxonomy has no 1T-prime distorted-octahedral entry. In chunk 019 the distorted phase is no longer a footnote -- Mo(1-x)Nb(x)Te2 runs to x = 0.8, and NbTe2 itself is the distorted-octahedral structure, so the majority of that host needs this id.

1T-prime (P2_1/m, centrosymmetric) and Td (Pmn2_1, polar) are the same layer with different stacking and convert into each other near 250 K in MoTe2. They are kept in one prototype because the layer, the coordination and the metal-metal chains are identical; the Td setting is what the polar-semimetal thermopower work measures, so a record that needs the distinction should say which setting in its basis.
Nb substitution for Mo stabilises the distorted phase at room temperature, which is why this prototype and the doping level are coupled in the Mo-Nb-Te host.

formula_archetype: AM2M(prime)Q4 (A = Ba or Sr; M = Cu or Ag; M(prime) = Sn or Ge; Q = S, Se or Te)
typical_space_group: I222 (23) for BaAg2SnSe4 per TEDesignLab; other members of the family are reported in related orthorhombic and trigonal settings, so the setting should be confirmed per compound

discriminate_from.stannite_kesterite: the closest relative in formula (A2BCX4 vs AB2CX4) but not in structure. Stannite and kesterite are ordered superstructures of sphalerite in which every cation is tetrahedral; the 1-2-1-4 compounds contain a large electropositive Ba that cannot occupy a tetrahedral site and instead sits in cavities of the M2M(prime)Q4 tetrahedral framework, so the framework is not a simple diamond-like cation ordering
discriminate_from.chalcopyrite: ternary, with no separate large-cation sublattice
discriminate_from.defect_chalcopyrite_ovc: the cation deficiency there is ordered vacancies in a diamond-like lattice; here the extra cation is a real, large, non-tetrahedral species
discriminate_from.caal2si2_zintl: also a large cation between covalent slabs, but the 1-2-2 polyanion is a trigonal layer of edge-sharing tetrahedra, a different topology and a different formula

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 019 for the Ag-Ba-Se-Sn host: all six samples are BaAg2SnSe4 and the paper is titled Origins of ultralow thermal conductivity in 1-2-1-4 quaternary selenides.

TEDesignLab carries BaAg2SnSe4 as PRIMARY with space group 23 and supplies no mp_id, so this is one of the 13 per cent of entries with ICSD backing and no Materials Project counterpart. Stage 2 will have to resolve the structure by another route.

The family is studied for very low lattice thermal conductivity, which is attributed to the rattling-like motion of the large A cation in the cavities of the tetrahedral framework -- so the large-cation-plus-framework description is the physically load-bearing part of the prototype, not bookkeeping.

formula_archetype: Ag10Te4X3 (X = Br, Cl)
typical_space_group: not settled by the references available here. The nearest Materials Project entry, Ag9Te4Br3 mp-676260, is given in P1 (1) at hull 0.062 and is a computed silver-deficient variant; the family is reported to disorder to a higher-symmetry silver-mobile phase on heating
representative_materials: Ag10Te4Br3 with Cl for Br and S or Se for Te

discriminate_from.argyrodite: the family it is most often lumped with. Argyrodites are A8BX6 with a tetrahedrally coordinated B cation at the centre of the anion framework; Ag10Te4Br3 has no such central cation and a different anion count, and its mobile-silver behaviour comes from a Te/halide substructure rather than from an argyrodite cage
discriminate_from.ag5te2cl_type: the other member of the same silver telluride halide family and the main thing to separate it from. The 5-2-1 composition is a different structure type; tell them apart by the Ag:Te:X ratio, which is 10:4:3 here and 5:2:1 there
discriminate_from.bcc_superionic: the high-temperature disordered end state, not the ambient ordered structure
discriminate_from.tetrahedrite: a copper antimony sulfosalt with a completely different framework

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 019 for the Ag-Br-Te host: all six compositions are Ag10Te4Br3 with partial anion substitution, from the Nilges work on resistivity switching combined with thermoelectric performance.

Silver-ion order-disorder transitions are reported in this family and the measured window here is 289-524 K, so a transition inside the window is likely. No temperature is established by either reference and none is asserted in the ledger; the paper would settle it, and this is flagged so the review queue picks it up.

structural_class is set to rocksalt-derived to sit beside ag2se_naumannite, cu2se_superionic and bcc_superionic -- the silver-mobile chalcogenides -- rather than because a rocksalt aristotype has been demonstrated. Stage 2 should revisit the class once the structure is resolved.

formula_archetype: Ag5Te2X (X = Cl, Br)
typical_space_group: Pnma (62), from the bromide analogue Ag5Te2Br mp-1215016 at hull 0.005; no chloride entry appears in either reference, so the setting should be confirmed

discriminate_from.ag10te4br3_type: the sibling compound in the same chemistry and the same publications. Separate them on the Ag:Te:X ratio, 5:2:1 here against 10:4:3 there; the two are distinct structures and should not be merged into one silver telluride halide label
discriminate_from.argyrodite: A8BX6 with a central tetrahedral cation, which this does not have
discriminate_from.ag2se_naumannite: a binary silver chalcogenide with no halide sublattice
discriminate_from.tetrahedrite: a different framework and a different chemistry

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 019 for the Ag-Cl-Te host: Ag5Te2Cl with partial S or Se for Te and Br for Cl, from the paper titled Reversible Property Switching, Thermoelectric Performance, and d10-d10 interactions in Ag5Te2Cl.

The reversible property switching named in that title is a structural or ionic transition, and the measured window is 297-505 K, so the measurement probably crosses it. No temperature is given by the references here, so none is recorded; the paper would settle it.

Kept separate from ag10te4br3_type on purpose. Both are silver-rich telluride halides from the same group, but a prototype is a structure type and these are two of them; merging them would repeat exactly the mistake the project is trying to undo.

formula_archetype: ABX with A = Ag, B = Cu, X = S or Se
typical_space_group: Cmc2_1 (36); the same ordered structure is also reported as Cmcm (63) and Pnma (62), and Materials Project flags its CuAgS mp-5014 Pnma entry AMBIGUOUS

discriminate_from.cu2se_superionic: the high-temperature end of the same material, not a different one. Stromeyerite is the ordered ambient phase with Ag and Cu on distinct, fully ordered sites; on heating AgCuS disorders in two steps and ends as the cubic cation-disordered superionic phase that cu2se_superionic describes, so a record spanning the transition needs both ids
discriminate_from.ag2se_naumannite: a binary Ag2X with no copper sublattice and a different ordered structure
discriminate_from.chalcopyrite: tetrahedral diamond-like ordering of a sphalerite lattice; stromeyerite has copper in trigonal and silver in near-linear coordination, not a diamond-like cation ordering
discriminate_from.argyrodite: A8BX6 with a central tetrahedral cation

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 019 for the Ag-Cu-S host: all six samples are AgCuS and the paper is titled The effect of order-disorder phase transitions and band gap evolution on the thermoelectric behaviour.

The order-disorder sequence is the reason the compound is studied: ordered orthorhombic stromeyerite converts to a hexagonal cation-disordered phase near 360 K and then to a cubic superionic phase near 440 K, both inside the 291-542 K measured window. The two temperatures come from materials knowledge, not from the references in the chunk file, and are recorded in the ledger at low-to-medium confidence.

The intermediate hexagonal phase has no taxonomy id. It is deliberately not proposed here: it is a transient disordering step between the two phases that do have ids, and inventing a prototype for it would add an entry no other host will ever use.

formula_archetype: A2X (A = Ag, X = S)
representative_materials: Ag2S with Se or Te on the chalcogen site

discriminate_from.ag2se_naumannite: the selenide sibling and the entry this would otherwise be forced into. Naumannite is orthorhombic P2_12_12_1 with a different ordered silver arrangement; acanthite is monoclinic P2_1/c. Same A2X composition, same superionic behaviour on heating, different ordered ambient structure, so the two ambient phases are not one prototype
discriminate_from.bcc_superionic: argentite, the body-centred cubic silver-disordered phase above about 450 K. Acanthite is the ordered low-temperature end of the same material, so a record whose window crosses the transition needs both ids in phases
discriminate_from.cu2se_superionic: the copper analogue, with its own ordered ambient structure
discriminate_from.argyrodite: A8BX6 with a central tetrahedrally coordinated cation, which a binary silver sulfide does not have

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 020 for the Ag-S host: all six samples are Ag2S or Ag2S with a few per cent excess sulfur, and Materials Project gives Ag2S P2_1/c (14) mp-610517 at hull 0.024 with 7 ICSD references as PRIMARY, which is acanthite.

TEDesignLab lists Ag2S only as P2_12_12_1 (19) mp-1095694 with 2 ICSD references and P2_1 (4) mp-31053 with 1, neither of which is the acanthite setting; the project precedence prefers TEDesignLab, but 7 ICSD references against 2 and the well-established monoclinic acanthite structure go the other way, and the ledger record says so rather than following the reference.

The acanthite to argentite transition near 450 K is the reason the compound is measured at all -- the superionic phase is what the nanocrystal paper in this host is about -- so this entry exists mainly so that the low-temperature half of that pair can be named.

formula_archetype: ABO2 (A = Li, B = Al or Ga)

discriminate_from.alpha_nafeo2_layered: alpha-LiAlO2 is the R-3m ordered-rocksalt layered polymorph of the same formula, with octahedral aluminium; the gamma form assigned here is a tetrahedral framework and is the phase used as a ceramic, so the polymorph has to be named rather than the formula
discriminate_from.wurtzite: beta-LiAlO2 is the wurtzite-derived orthorhombic Pna2_1 polymorph -- also tetrahedral, but a hexagonal-close-packed oxygen array rather than the gamma framework
discriminate_from.spinel: LiAl5O8 in the same binary is the spinel-related compound; it is a different composition with octahedral aluminium
discriminate_from.diamond_cubic: LiAl itself is the NaTl-type intermetallic of this element pair and has no oxygen at all -- the distinction matters here because the composition string that produced this host lost its oxygen

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 020 for the Al-Li host. The single composition is written LiAl02, with the letter O typed as a zero, and the paper is titled Effects of Fast Neutron Irradiation on Thermal Conductivity of Li2O and LiAlO2 -- so the material is lithium aluminate and the host key Al-Li is a parse artifact, not a lithium aluminium alloy.

Because the oxygen is missing from the composition string, both reference blocks for this host return Li-Al intermetallics (LiAl Fd-3m mp-1067 with 26 ICSD references and so on). None of them describes the measured material, and no mp_id is recorded in the ledger for that reason.

gamma-LiAlO2 is the polymorph used as a tritium breeder ceramic and the one a 1988 fusion-materials irradiation study would have measured, but the paper has not been read, so the assignment is recorded at medium confidence and the alpha and beta polymorphs are listed as alternatives rather than dismissed.

formula_archetype: RT2B2 (R = rare earth, T = Ir, Rh or Ru)
typical_space_group: Fddd (70) per Materials Project for Ce(BIr)2; the family is also reported in monoclinic settings, so the setting should be confirmed per compound

discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: the entry this would otherwise be forced into, and the one it must be kept apart from. Many RT2B2 borides are genuine ThCr2Si2-type I4/mmm compounds, but the iridium member is not: the only entry at this exact composition is Fddd (70) with 2 ICSD references, an orthorhombic structure with boron pairs in a different framework, so using the 122 id here would assert a tetragonal structure the references contradict
discriminate_from.borocarbide_1221: RM2B2C adds a carbon layer to the 122 block and is tetragonal I4/mmm; this is the carbon-free ternary and a different symmetry
discriminate_from.alb2: a planar boron net with no transition-metal boron framework
discriminate_from.cab6_hexaboride: a boron octahedron cage framework at AB6, not an RT2B2 line compound

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 020 for the B-Ce-Ir host: all six samples are CeIr2B2 and the paper is on ferromagnetic ordering in CeIr2B2 studied by transport, magnetization and specific heat.

Materials Project gives Ce(BIr)2 Fddd (70) mp-8680 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references as PRIMARY, alongside three other Ce-Ir-B line compounds at different stoichiometries (CeB2Ir3, Ce(BIr)4, Ce2B2Ir5). The Fddd entry is the composition measured here.

The structure has not been read out of the paper and two ICSD references is thin, so the ledger record is low-to-medium confidence. The entry is worth having anyway because it marks a real gap: the taxonomy treats RT2B2 as ThCr2Si2 territory and the iridium borides are not that.

formula_archetype: ACu4X3 (A = Ba or Sr, X = S or Se)

discriminate_from.bacu2s2_layered: the other compound in the same host and the same papers. ACu2X2 has a puckered single CuX layer between the alkaline-earth cations; ACu4X3 is copper-richer, with a thicker CuX slab of a different connectivity and a fixed 4:3 ratio. They are two structures, not two compositions of one, so the Ba-Cu-S host is flagged mixed rather than given one label
discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: a 1:2:2 tetragonal structure, a different formula and a different symmetry
discriminate_from.fese_pbo: anti-PbO tetrahedral layers appear in both families, but this is a ternary with a large cation between the slabs, not a binary
discriminate_from.bi_chalcogenide_complex: a line compound with a modest cell, not a module-built large-cell chalcogenide

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 020 for the Ba-Cu-S host, where two of the six samples are BaCu4S3 and BaCu3.96S3 from the paper titled A p-type thermoelectric material BaCu4S3 with high electronic band degeneracy.

TEDesignLab carries BaCu4S3 Pnma (62) mp-654109 at hull 0.019 with 2 ICSD references as PRIMARY, and a Cmcm (63) setting mp-27424 at hull 0.000 with 1 reference; the Pnma setting is taken as the prototype and the Cmcm one noted as unresolved between a genuine polymorph and an alternative description.
The selenide BaCu4Se3 is studied in the same thermoelectric context, so the entry is expected to be reused rather than being a single-host convenience.

display_name: Hybrid organic-inorganic halide perovskite (ABX3, A = molecular cation)
formula_archetype: ABX3 with A a molecular cation (CH3NH3, HC(NH2)2), B = Pb or Sn, X = I, Br or Cl
typical_space_group: Pm-3m (221) cubic above about 327 K; I4/mcm (140) tetragonal between about 162 and 327 K; Pnma (62) orthorhombic below about 162 K

discriminate_from.perovskite: the oxide archetype. The framework topology is the same corner-sharing BX3 network, but the A site holds a rotating molecular cation rather than a spherical metal ion, the anion is a halide, and the whole compound is soft and low-melting -- which is why it has three phases inside an ordinary transport window and why the taxonomy should not file it as an ABO3 tilt variant
discriminate_from.formate_mof_perovskite: also a hybrid ABX3, but the X bridge is a polyatomic formate linker rather than a single halide ion, giving a much larger cell
discriminate_from.bii3_layered_trihalide: a layered binary trihalide with no A cation and van der Waals gaps, not a 3D corner-sharing framework
discriminate_from.double_perovskite: the halide double perovskites (Cs2AgBiBr6 and relatives) are the B-site ordered members of this family; use that id when two different B cations order

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 020 for the C-H-I-N-Pb host: three samples are CH3NH3PbI3 and three are the same with one, three and five per cent BiI3 added, from two papers on doping optimization and on bismuth doping-induced stable Seebeck effect in MAPbI3.

The three settings listed under typical_space_group are one distortion series of one prototype, in the same sense as the WO3 series already carried by reo3_wo3, not three prototypes. The measured window here is 30-401 K and crosses both transitions, so the ledger record lists all three as phases with the single id.

Materials Project returns only computed hydrogen-ordered approximants for this chemistry (mp-995214, mp-1194995 and similar, all with one or no ICSD reference and settings that reflect a frozen methylammonium orientation), so no mp_id is recorded. The disorder of the molecular cation is physical, not a defect of the entries.
Four of the six samples are films, where a metastable setting can be held that bulk material would not keep; that is flagged in the ledger record rather than resolved here.

formula_archetype: M[A(n-1)BnO(3n+1)] with M = K, Rb or Cs and n = 2, 3 or 4
typical_space_group: Cmcm (63) and related orthorhombic settings, n-dependent

discriminate_from.ruddlesden_popper: the layered perovskite family the taxonomy already has, and the one to separate this from. Ruddlesden-Popper slabs are offset by half a cell and separated by a rocksalt AO double layer; Dion-Jacobson slabs sit directly above one another with a single alkali layer between them, which is what makes the alkali exchangeable and the slab exfoliable. An n = 3 Ruddlesden-Popper phase and an n = 3 Dion-Jacobson phase have the same slab and different interlayers
discriminate_from.aurivillius: the interlayer is a Bi2O2 slab rather than a single alkali layer
discriminate_from.layered_double_perovskite: A-site cation ordering inside a continuous 3D framework, with no interlayer gap at all
discriminate_from.perovskite: the n to infinity end member with no interlayer

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 020 for the Ca-K-Nb-O host: all six samples are KCa2Nb3O10 and the paper is titled Transport properties of Li intercalated KCa2Nb3O10.

Materials Project gives KCa2Nb3O10 Cmc2_1 (36) mp-1223594 at hull 0.012 with no ICSD reference; the setting is therefore not settled by the references and the entry records the family rather than one space group.

The interlayer alkali is the point of the family: it is exchangeable and intercalatable, which is exactly what the paper measures, so stage 3 should treat intercalated lithium as a compositional variable of the interlayer rather than as a dopant on a perovskite site.

display_name: M7O12 rhombohedral ordered anion-deficient fluorite (In4Sn3O12 / Zr3Sc4O12 delta phase)
formula_archetype: M7O12, i.e. MO(12/7), a fluorite MO2 with one anion in seven ordered as a vacancy pair along the body diagonal

discriminate_from.fluorite_oxide: the parent MO2 with a full anion array and no vacancy order. The delta phase is what that array becomes once one anion in seven is removed and the vacancies order on the rhombohedral axis, which lowers the symmetry from Fm-3m to R-3 and fixes the cation ratio at 7:12 rather than leaving it continuous
discriminate_from.bixbyite: the other ordered anion-deficient fluorite in this system, M2O3 = M32O48, one anion in four removed and ordered cubically in Ia-3. In2O3 itself is bixbyite; adding Sn and Sb pushes the composition off M2O3 towards MO2 and the vacancy order changes with it
discriminate_from.pyrochlore: A2B2O7 = M4O7, one anion in eight removed, ordered in Fd-3m, and requiring two cations of markedly different size on distinct A and B sites. The delta phase keeps all cations on one octahedral-to-sevenfold site set
discriminate_from.homologous_inmo3_zno: the other indium oxide family in thermoelectrics, built from InO2 layers alternating with (M,Zn)O blocks rather than from a vacancy-ordered fluorite

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 021 for the In-O-Sb-Sn host: all six compositions are In5SnSbO12 with gallium substituting for indium, and the paper is titled Improved densification and thermoelectric performance of In5SnSbO12.

The chunk file returns no TEDesignLab and no Materials Project entry for this host, so nothing in the references was available to test the assignment against. The identification rests on the cation-to-anion ratio: 7 cations to 12 oxygens is the delta phase stoichiometry, and In4Sn3O12 is the established rhombohedral R-3 phase of the In2O3-SnO2 system at exactly that ratio. In5SnSbO12 replaces two of its tin atoms with one indium and one antimony, keeping the ratio and the charge balance. It should be checked against the diffraction pattern in the paper before the entry is accepted.

The family matters beyond this host because it is the ordered middle of the In2O3-SnO2 join that carries ITO: the same chemistry gives bixbyite at M2O3, this phase at M7O12 and rutile-type SnO2 at MO2, and the taxonomy had entries for the two ends but not the middle.

Stage 3 should read the vacancy order as the structural feature it is, not as oxygen non-stoichiometry: the missing anions are ordered and part of the prototype, so an oxygen count below 2 per cation is not a defect concentration to be tuned.

formula_archetype: AM2O6 (A = Zn, Mg, Ni, Co, Fe; M = Sb, Ta, Nb)
typical_space_group: P4_2/mnm (136), with the c axis tripled relative to rutile

discriminate_from.rutile: the parent MO2 and the entry this would otherwise be forced into. Trirutile keeps the rutile framework of edge- and corner-sharing octahedra and even keeps the space group symbol, but two cation species order along c in the repeating sequence A-M-M, which triples the c axis and fixes the composition at AM2O6. Filing it as rutile would assert a single disordered cation site and lose the stoichiometry
discriminate_from.spinel: Zn7Sb2O12 in the same chemistry is the spinel-related phase, a different compound at a different Zn:Sb ratio; it is the reason the O-Sb-Zn host is flagged mixed rather than an alternative description of the same material
discriminate_from.pyrochlore: A2B2O7, a different cation-to-anion ratio with eight-coordinate A cations, not an octahedral rutile framework
discriminate_from.hollandite: also a tetragonal MO2-derived framework, but built from double octahedral chains enclosing tunnels that host large cations, rather than from cation ordering on the rutile sites

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 022 for the O-Sb-Zn host: four of the five compositions are ZnSb2O6 or Zn(1-x)MxSb2O6 with M = Al or In, from the paper on thermoelectric properties of Zn1-xMxSb2O6.

Materials Project carries Zn(SbO3)2 P4_2/mnm (136) mp-3188 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references, which is the trirutile at the measured composition. The entry it ranks PRIMARY for this host, Zn(SbO2)2 P4_2/mbc (135) mp-5388 with 9 references, is ZnSb2O4 -- a different compound with Sb(III) rather than Sb(V) -- so the reference primary is answering a different question and is not followed.

Trirutile ZnSb2O6 and MgSb2O6 are wide-gap transparent conducting oxides doped n-type on the divalent site, which is exactly what the Al and In substitutions in this host are doing, so the ordering is load-bearing for stage 3 as well as for stage 2.

formula_archetype: AB2O6 (A = K, Rb, Cs, Tl; B = Os, or a Nb/Ta/W pair in the defect pyrochlore oxides)

discriminate_from.pyrochlore: the A2B2O7 parent, and the entry this would otherwise be filed under. The corner-sharing B2O6 octahedral network is identical in both. What differs is everything inside it: the interpenetrating A2O-prime sublattice of the full pyrochlore is gone, the O-prime site is empty and only one A cation in two remains, sitting in an oversized cage it does not fill. The formula archetype is AB2O6 rather than A2B2O7, and the rattling of that loose cation is what the superconductivity and the low lattice thermal conductivity in this family are attributed to, so the difference is physical rather than bookkeeping
discriminate_from.hollandite: another oxide framework built to host loosely bound cations, but from edge-sharing double octahedral chains forming one-dimensional tunnels, not the three-dimensional pyrochlore network
discriminate_from.spinel: AB2O4 -- one fewer oxygen, and a tetrahedrally coordinated A site rather than an oversized cage
discriminate_from.clathrate_i: the same rattling-guest physics in a covalent tetrahedral framework rather than an octahedral oxide one
discriminate_from.reo3_wo3: a corner-sharing octahedral oxide network with no guest cation at all

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 022 for the O-Os-Rb host: all six samples are RbOs2O6 and both papers are explicitly on beta-pyrochlore oxides -- chemical trends of superconducting properties in pyrochlore oxides, and high-pressure effects on the superconductivity of beta-pyrochlore oxides.

Materials Project gives Rb(OsO3)2 Fd-3m (227) mp-5050 at hull 0.000 with 12 ICSD references as PRIMARY, which is strong support for the framework and the space group; what it cannot say is that the A site is half-empty, which is the point of the entry.

The taxonomy already carried pyrochlore with formula_archetype A2B2O7. Adding the defect variant rather than stretching that archetype keeps the two separable, in the same way filled and unfilled skutterudite are kept separate.

formula_archetype: RE3MO7 (RE = rare earth; M = Nb, Ta, Sb, Mo, Ru, Re)
typical_space_group: Cmcm (63) for the larger rare earths; C222_1 and P2_12_12_1 settings are also reported across the family, and the smallest rare earths take a disordered defect-fluorite Fm-3m form instead, so the setting has to be confirmed per compound

discriminate_from.pyrochlore: the trap worth naming. RE3MO7 is M4O7 on a per-cation basis, exactly the same four-cations-to-seven-anions ratio as A2B2O7 pyrochlore, and both are ordered anion-deficient fluorites -- so the stoichiometry alone does not separate them. The cation ordering does: pyrochlore needs two cations in a 2:2 ratio and markedly different sizes on distinct cubic A and B sites, while the weberite type orders 3:1 into alternating chains of MO6 octahedra and eight-coordinate REO8 polyhedra, which is orthorhombic
discriminate_from.fluorite_oxide: the MO2 parent with a full anion array and no ordering of cations or vacancies. The distinction is not automatic here -- the small-rare-earth members of this family really do adopt the disordered defect fluorite, so the ordering must be checked rather than inferred from the formula
discriminate_from.m7o12_delta_fluorite: the other ordered anion-deficient fluorite proposed in this project, at M7O12 with one anion in seven removed and rhombohedral R-3 order. Different vacancy count, different order, different symmetry
discriminate_from.perovskite: not a corner-sharing ABO3 network; the octahedra here are isolated into chains by the RE polyhedra

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 022 for the O-Sm-Ta host: all six compositions are Sm3TaO7 with 0 to 10 per cent ZrO2 added, from the paper on thermophysical properties of ZrO2-Sm3TaO7 ceramics.

Materials Project gives Sm3TaO7 Cmcm (63) mp-1192238 at hull 0.003 with 1 ICSD reference, which matches both the composition and the expected weberite-type setting, though a single reference is thin support.

The family is studied for very low and weakly temperature-dependent thermal conductivity as a thermal barrier coating, which is the reason a 371-1173 K measurement exists at all; the low conductivity is attributed to the cation and vacancy disorder the ordering leaves behind, so the prototype and the property are linked.

formula_archetype: AM10P4 (A = Sr, and by analogy Ca or Ba; M = Pt)
typical_space_group: not established by anything available here. Neither TEDesignLab nor Materials Project carries an entry at this composition, and the paper reporting the compound describes it as a complex new structure type. This field must be filled from the paper before the entry is accepted

discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: the usual home for ternary alkaline-earth transition-metal phosphides. This is far more metal-rich, at 1:10:4 rather than 1:2:2, and is not a layered 122 structure
discriminate_from.zrcusias_1111: the other common layered pnictide family, also at a much lower metal-to-phosphorus ratio
discriminate_from.cacu5: a metal-rich AM5 intermetallic framework, but binary, with no covalent phosphorus sublattice threaded through it
discriminate_from.unresolved_crystalline: the honest alternative to this entry, and worth stating. The host could have been parked there. It is not, because the compound is named, single-phase and its structure type is published -- what is missing is the space group, not the identity. The entry therefore records a gap with a label rather than without one, and should be reviewed on that basis

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 022 for the P-Pt-Sr host: all six samples are SrPt10P4, from the paper titled Superconductivity in the ternary compound SrPt10P4 with complex new structure type.

Materials Project returns three other Sr-Pt-P line compounds -- Sr(P3Pt2)2 C2/c mp-8507, Sr(PPt3)2 Pa-3 mp-1194990 and SrPPt P-6m2 mp-1217967, each with at most 1 ICSD reference -- and none at the 1:10:4 composition. No mp_id is recorded in the ledger for that reason.

This is the thinnest entry proposed so far in this project and is flagged as such deliberately: it has one member, no space group and no reference support. It exists so that the host is not mislabelled as a 122 phosphide, and it should either be completed from the paper or rejected at v4 review.

formula_archetype: MP2 (M = W, Mo)

discriminate_from.osge2_monoclinic: the centrosymmetric C2/m relative, and in this chemistry the other polymorph of the very same compound -- Materials Project carries both P2W Cmc2_1 mp-11328 and P2W C2/m mp-11329. The distinction is the entire reason this entry exists: only the noncentrosymmetric Cmc2_1 form is the type-II Weyl semimetal whose extreme magnetoresistance, hydrodynamic electron flow and Wiedemann-Franz violation are what the papers in this host measure. Assigning the C2/m entry would name a structure with a different topology of band crossings
discriminate_from.marcasite: an orthorhombic Pnnm MX2 built from edge-sharing octahedra with anion dimers; a different framework and a different coordination
discriminate_from.mnp_b31: the MnP-type monophosphide. WP itself adopts it, and it is what the reference block ranks first for this host, but it is a different formula
discriminate_from.pyrite: cubic MX2 with isolated anion dimers in corner-sharing octahedra

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 022 for the P-W host: all six samples are WP2 and both papers are on the Weyl semimetal -- thermal and electrical signatures of a hydrodynamic electron fluid, and departure from the Wiedemann-Franz law in WP2.

The Materials Project block ranks PW Pnma (62) mp-2420 with 5 ICSD references first for this host. That is tungsten monophosphide and not the compound measured; within the diphosphide the Cmc2_1 setting mp-11328 carries 3 ICSD references and the C2/m setting mp-11329 carries 2.

The two settings are recorded as separate prototypes rather than as one family because they differ by inversion symmetry, and in a Weyl semimetal inversion symmetry is what decides whether the band crossings exist. This is the same reasoning that kept 1T-prime and its polar Td stacking together in mote2_1t_prime -- there the layer is identical, here the symmetry is not.

display_name: HfCuSi2-type 112 layered pnictide with square anion nets
formula_archetype: AMPn2 (A = Ca, Sr, Ba, Eu or rare earth; M = Zn, Cu, Mn, Ag; Pn = Sb or Bi)
typical_space_group: P4/nmm (129) for the ideal tetragonal form; Pnma (62) and related orthorhombic settings where the pnictogen square net distorts, which is the setting Materials Project gives for SrZnSb2 mp-12275

discriminate_from.zrcusias_1111: the parent of the family and the entry this would otherwise be forced into. The 1111 structure puts an oxide or fluoride layer between the anti-PbO MPn slabs; the 112 compounds drop that layer, and what sits between the slabs instead is a flat square net of the pnictogen itself. That net is the electronically interesting part -- it carries the Dirac dispersion these compounds are studied for -- so merging the two would erase exactly the feature that distinguishes them
discriminate_from.caal2si2_zintl: the other compound in the Sb-Sr-Zn host. SrZn2Sb2 is the trigonal CaAl2Si2 type, a corrugated Zn2Sb2 slab of edge-sharing tetrahedra with no square net and a different formula. The two are why that host is flagged mixed rather than given one label
discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: also a tetragonal layered alkaline-earth pnictide, but with two transition metals per formula, no separate anion square net, and X-X bonds between the slabs
discriminate_from.fese_pbo: the anti-PbO MPn slab is the same building block, taken on its own without the alkaline-earth and square-net layers

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 022 for the Sb-Sr-Zn host: three of the six samples are SrZnSb2, from the paper titled Transport properties of the layered Zintl compound SrZnSb2. The other three are SrZn2Sb2 and are the CaAl2Si2 type, which the taxonomy already carries.

Materials Project gives SrZnSb2 Pnma (62) mp-12275 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference. The orthorhombic setting rather than the ideal P4/nmm reflects a real Peierls-like distortion of the antimony square net, which is common across the family and should not be read as a different prototype.
The 112 pnictides are studied both as Zintl thermoelectrics and as Dirac semimetals, and the square net is the reason for both, so the entry is expected to be reused well beyond this host.

formula_archetype: Al3Mg2, with a homogeneity range around Al3.2Mg2
typical_space_group: Fd-3m (227), with roughly 1168 atoms in the cubic cell, part of them on partially occupied and positionally disordered sites

discriminate_from.laves_phase: the closest structural relative. The Samson phase is built largely from Friauf polyhedra, the same coordination unit as the MgCu2 C15 Laves phase, but assembled into a cell two orders of magnitude larger with intrinsic partial occupancy. A Laves phase has 24 atoms in its cell and a fixed AB2 composition; this has over a thousand and a homogeneity range
discriminate_from.quasicrystal_approximant: the other entry a giant-cell aluminium alloy could be dropped into, and the one to be careful with. The Samson phase is a genuine periodic crystal with a defined space group, not an approximant standing in for an aperiodic structure, and the binary Al-Mg system produces no icosahedral phase without a third element
discriminate_from.solid_solution_alloy: the dilute Al-Mg and Mg-Al engineering alloys that share this host -- ordinary substitutional fcc and hcp solid solutions. They are why the host is flagged mixed
discriminate_from.high_entropy_alloy: a multi-principal-element random solid solution on a simple lattice; this is an ordered giant cell in a binary

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 022 for the Al-Mg host: two of the five samples are Al3Mg2, from the paper titled Magnetic and transport properties of the giant-unit-cell Al3.26Mg2 compound.

Materials Project ranks Mg17Al12 I-43m (217) mp-2151 with 5 ICSD references first for this host. That is the gamma phase, an alpha-Mn-type structure at a different composition, and not the beta phase measured here; no entry in the block is at Al3Mg2.

The giant cell with its partial occupancy is why the compound has a very low, glass-like lattice thermal conductivity despite being a simple binary of two light metals, which is the reason it is measured in a thermoelectric context. Recording it as a solid solution or a Laves phase would lose that.

display_name: MAX phase Mn+1AXn nanolaminate carbide and nitride
formula_archetype: Mn+1AXn with n = 1, 2 or 3 (M = early transition metal; A = Al, Si, Ga, Ge, Sn, In; X = C or N)
typical_space_group: P6_3/mmc (194) for every member; n counts the MX layers stacked between A planes and changes the cell length, not the symmetry

discriminate_from.zrc_al3c2_homologous: the closest entry already in the taxonomy and the one a MAX phase would otherwise be forced into. Both are layered ternary aluminium carbides built by interleaving a binary carbide slab with aluminium, but the (MC)nAl3C2 series puts Al3C2 blocks with carbon inside them between the slabs and sits in P6_3mc, while a MAX phase puts a single flat plane of bare A atoms between MX slabs in P6_3/mmc. The A plane is the whole point: it is the weakly bound layer that gives the kink-band plasticity, the machinability and the anisotropic transport
discriminate_from.rocksalt_nitride_carbide: the MX slab on its own. TiN and TiC are the binary rocksalt carbides and nitrides, and a MAX phase is those slabs cut into two- or three-octahedra-thick layers and separated by aluminium. Compositions in a host can sit in either, which is why Al-N-Ti is flagged mixed rather than given one label
discriminate_from.wurtzite: AlN and the (Al,Ti)N solid solutions taken from it are simple tetrahedral nitrides with no transition-metal carbide slab at all; they share the Al-N-Ti host but nothing structural
discriminate_from.alb2: a layered hexagonal intermetallic in P6/mmm with a graphene-like boron net, not a rocksalt-derived MX slab

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 023 for the Al-N-Ti host: Ti2AlN is the 211 MAX phase and Ti4AlN2.9 is the 413 member of the same series, and Materials Project gives Ti2AlN P6_3/mmc (194) mp-1080056 at hull 0.000 with 6 ICSD references.

The structural_class is recorded as layered van der Waals to sit alongside zrc_al3c2_homologous, but that label is wrong about the bonding and is flagged here rather than left to mislead: the M-A bond is metallic, the layers do not exfoliate mechanically, and it is chemical etching of the A layer that produces MXenes. The class vocabulary has no better member; the taxonomy may want a layered metallic or nanolaminate class at v4.

MAX phases are a large family with real thermoelectric literature and they appear in at least two hosts in this chunk alone, Ti2AlN in Al-N-Ti and Cr2AlC in the composite measured in C-Cr, so the entry is expected to be reused.

formula_archetype: RE2O3 and An2O3 (RE = La through Nd and the larger trivalent actinides)

discriminate_from.bixbyite: the C-type sesquioxide, cubic Ia-3, which is the same formula in a different structure and is the reason this entry has to exist separately. C-type is a fluorite with a quarter of the anions removed and ordered, six-coordinate and cubic; A-type is seven-coordinate and trigonal. Which one forms is decided by cation size and by temperature, with the larger rare earths and the higher temperatures favouring A-type, so the formula alone never settles it
discriminate_from.fluorite_oxide: the tetravalent dioxide MO2 with a complete anion array. The pair matters in the actinides in particular, where AmO2 and Am2O3 sit in one host and differ by oxidation state as well as structure
discriminate_from.corundum: the other common sesquioxide structure, taken by the small trivalent cations Al, Cr and Fe. Six-coordinate in a hexagonally close-packed anion array rather than seven-coordinate in the A-type layer stacking

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 023 for the Am-O host, where Am2O3 is measured alongside AmO2 and neither reference block returns anything for the chemistry.

The taxonomy already carries bixbyite for the C-type sesquioxide and fluorite_oxide for the dioxide, so A-type was the missing third member of a set that is otherwise complete. Without it any A-type sesquioxide is either mislabelled as C-type or parked in unresolved_crystalline.

Which polymorph Am2O3 takes is temperature-dependent and was not determinable from the composition here, so the Am-O record names this entry as an alternative alongside bixbyite rather than asserting one.

formula_archetype: (AE2MO3)(FeAs) and the related 22323 and 42622 members, built by stacking a perovskite oxide block on an anti-PbO FeAs layer

discriminate_from.zrcusias_1111: the entry this family would otherwise be forced into, and the closest relative. Both put an oxide layer between anti-PbO FeAs slabs, but in the 1111 structure that layer is a single fluorite-like LnO sheet, while here it is a perovskite block two or more octahedra thick. The block is what pushes the FeAs layers apart into genuine two-dimensionality and what carries a second magnetic sublattice in the vanadium member, so merging them would lose both
discriminate_from.fese_pbo: the FeAs or FeSe slab taken on its own with nothing between the layers. It is the shared building block of this whole family rather than a competing assignment
discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: the other iron arsenide superconductor family, BaFe2As2 and relatives. Same FeAs slab again, but separated by a bare alkaline-earth layer with no oxide at all, and body-centred tetragonal rather than primitive
discriminate_from.ruddlesden_popper: an oxide-only perovskite and rocksalt intergrowth. The perovskite block here is the same kind of unit, but what it alternates with is a pnictide layer, not a rocksalt oxide layer, and the conduction happens in the pnictide

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 023 for the As-Fe-O-Sr-V host: four of the five samples are Sr2VFeAsO3 and both papers are on superconductivity in perovskite-related iron-based materials.

Materials Project gives Sr2VFeAsO3 P4/nmm (129) mp-1106248 with 3 ICSD references, which confirms both the composition and the space group; the hull distance of 0.087 is unremarkable for a layered intergrowth and should not be read as instability.

This family is studied because the perovskite block can be varied independently of the FeAs layer, which separates the structural and electronic variables in a way the 1111 and 122 families cannot, so it is worth a prototype of its own rather than a footnote on zrcusias_1111.

formula_archetype: RM4X (R = rare earth or actinide; M = Co, Ni, Cu; X = B)
typical_space_group: P6/mmm (191) for the ideal CeCo4B type. UNi4B itself is the reason this field carries a caveat: it has been refined in the polar hexagonal P6_3mc and later in a larger orthorhombic Cmcm superstructure arising from ordering of the nickel and boron, so the setting has to be taken from the paper rather than from the type

discriminate_from.cacu5: the aristotype, and the entry this would otherwise be folded into. CeCo4B is CaCu5 with boron replacing one transition metal in every second basal layer, which doubles the c axis and creates two inequivalent metal sites. Both the doubling and the site splitting matter here: the partial magnetic ordering of UNi4B, in which a third of the uranium moments stay paramagnetic down to the lowest temperatures, is a consequence of that site inequivalence
discriminate_from.prni2al3_ordered_cacu5: the other ordered CaCu5 derivative already in the taxonomy. There the ordering is between two metals in the same basal plane and the cell is not doubled along c; here a metalloid enters alternate planes and it is
discriminate_from.alb2: a hexagonal layered intermetallic with a boron net, but AB2 rather than RM4X and with no CaCu5 parentage

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 023 for the B-Ni-U host: all five samples are UNi4B, from papers on large thermoelectric power in metallic cerium and uranium compounds and on the magnetic phase diagram of hexagonal UNi4B.

Materials Project returns nothing at this composition for the host. The two entries it does give, U2(Ni7B2)3 Fm-3m mp-10130 and UNiB4 I4/mmm mp-972320, are different stoichiometries with one ICSD reference each, so no mp_id is recorded in the ledger.

The entry is proposed at medium confidence in its own space group. What is certain is the structure type and its CaCu5 parentage; what is not is which of the reported settings UNi4B takes, and that should be resolved from the literature before v4 rather than by choosing the ideal type by default.

formula_archetype: M3C2 (M = Cr, and by extension the Re3B-related M3X2 carbides)

discriminate_from.rocksalt_nitride_carbide: the entry any carbide is at risk of being swept into. TiC, TaC and their nitrides are cubic rocksalt with carbon filling every octahedral hole of a close-packed metal array; Cr3C2 is orthorhombic with carbon in trigonal prisms, a metal-rich composition and a lower symmetry. Chromium does form a metastable rocksalt CrC, which Materials Project lists at mp-579 with 3 ICSD references and a hull distance of 0.256, so the two really do coexist in this chemistry and the distinction has to be made rather than assumed
discriminate_from.max_phase_mn1axn: the other carbide proposed from this chunk, and the second phase in one of the C-Cr compositions, which contains Cr2AlC. A MAX phase is a layered ternary with aluminium planes; this is a binary with no A element
discriminate_from.mnp_b31: the other common low-symmetry Pnma binary of a transition metal with a light element, at M:X of 1:1 rather than 3:2 and with a different prism connectivity

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 023 for the C-Cr host: Cr3C2 is measured pure and as the matrix of SiC and Cr7C3 composites, and Materials Project gives Cr3C2 Pnma (62) mp-20937 at hull 0.000 with 9 ICSD references.

The chromium carbides are a series -- Cr23C6 in Fm-3m with 11 ICSD references, Cr7C3 and Cr3C in Pnma with 4 and 3 -- and this entry deliberately names only Cr3C2 rather than the whole series, because Cr23C6 is a genuinely different structure and lumping them would repeat the mistake of a single carbide label.

Cr3C2 is measured thermoelectrically mainly as a wear-resistant coating material rather than as a thermoelectric candidate, so the entry may see little reuse; it exists so the host is not parked in unresolved_crystalline or mislabelled as a rocksalt carbide.

display_name: CeNiC2-type ternary carbide with carbon dimers
formula_archetype: RTC2 (R = rare earth; T = Ni, Co, Fe, Ru)

discriminate_from.borocarbide_1221: the other layered rare-earth transition-metal compound with a light-element dimer, LuNi2B2C, where the dimer is boron in a tetragonal body-centred cell. Here the dimer is C2 in a noncentrosymmetric orthorhombic cell at a different stoichiometry
discriminate_from.rocksalt_nitride_carbide: carbon here is not an interstitial in a metal array but part of a covalently bonded C2 unit with its own intramolecular bond, which is what makes the carbon sublattice distortable and lets a charge density wave form
discriminate_from.alb2: a hexagonal AB2 intermetallic with a planar net of light atoms; this is orthorhombic with discrete dimers rather than a net

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 023 for the C-Ni-Sm host: all five samples are SmNiC2, from the paper on magnon gap formation and charge density wave effect on thermoelectric power. Materials Project gives SmNiC2 Amm2 (38) mp-999144 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references, matching the CeNiC2 type.

The noncentrosymmetric Amm2 setting is not incidental. The RNiC2 series is studied precisely because it carries a charge density wave -- near 148 K in SmNiC2, inside the measured 10-299 K window -- and the transition is unusual in being suppressed rather than enhanced by the ferromagnetic ordering below it.

The CDW distortion produces a superstructure with a lower symmetry than Amm2, so a member measured across the transition strictly has two structures. That is recorded as a note here rather than as a separate prototype, because the distortion is a modulation of this structure, not a different type.

formula_archetype: MBi4X7 (M = Mn, Fe; X = S, Se)

discriminate_from.mnsb2se4_type: the nearest entry in the taxonomy and the one this would otherwise be forced into. Both are monoclinic C2/m chalcogenides of a divalent transition metal with a group 15 element, but the ratio is fixed at 1:2 there and 1:4 here, which is a different member of the same homologous construction and a different slab thickness. The taxonomy entry states the 1:2 ratio as part of its definition, so extending it would contradict its own discriminant
discriminate_from.bi_chalcogenide_complex: the catch-all for large-cell alkali bismuth chalcogenides, where every composition is effectively its own structure. This is a defined line compound with a named type and a reference structure, so it does not belong in a bucket whose purpose is to hold the ones that cannot be typed
discriminate_from.tetradymite: Bi2S3 and Bi2Se3 chemistry is adjacent, but the tetradymite quintuple layer is rhombohedral with van der Waals gaps; here the bismuth sulfide slabs are stitched together by octahedrally coordinated manganese and there is no gap
discriminate_from.cdi2_1t: the other layered structure a divalent metal chalcogenide can take, with a single octahedral sheet. The slabs here are several octahedra thick and NaCl-like in their interior

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 023 for the Bi-Mn-S host: four compositions are MnBi4S7 or close to it, and Materials Project gives MnBi4S7 C2/m (12) mp-1095372 at hull 0.010 with 1 ICSD reference. The lead paper is titled XBi4S7 (X = Mn, Fe), which names the family directly.

The structural_class is recorded as rocksalt-derived because the slabs are NaCl-type blocks in their interior, in the manner of the pavonite and lillianite sulfosalt homologous series; the entry may be better placed as one member of a homologous series at v4 review, alongside homologous_tetradymite and gst_homologous.
The second paper measures MnBi4S7-7xSe7x, so the selenide member is already in the dataset and the formula archetype is written to include it.

formula_archetype: A2MO2Cu2X2 (A = Sr, Ba; M = Mn, Co, Ni, Zn; X = S, Se)

discriminate_from.zrcusias_1111: the nearest entry in v3 and the one this host would otherwise be forced into. Both alternate an antifluorite Cu2X2 layer with an oxide layer, but the 1111 type puts a single fluorite-like REO sheet against it at the formula REMXO. Here the oxide block is a K2NiF4-like A2MO2 slab whose M site is a square-planar sheet of a second transition metal, and that sheet is where the magnetism and much of the transport live
discriminate_from.ruddlesden_popper: the A2MO4 oxide block on its own. This structure is that block with the apical oxygens removed and an antifluorite Cu2S2 layer inserted in their place, so the M site is coordinated by oxygen only while the sulfur belongs to a separate copper layer
discriminate_from.bacu2s2_layered: the other layered A-Cu-S entry, with no oxide layer, no second transition metal and a divalent A cation

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 024 for the Co-Cu-O-S-Sr host: all five compositions are Sr2-xCaxCu2CoO2S2 and the paper is on the electronic nature of the layered oxysulfide Sr2-xCaxCu2CoO2S2 with CoO2 planes. Nothing in v3 covers an A2MO2Cu2X2 intergrowth.

What makes the family worth its own entry for thermoelectrics is that two conducting sublattices coexist -- a square-planar CoO2 sheet and a Cu2S2 layer -- so a Seebeck coefficient here is a parallel-conduction measurement rather than a single-band one.
The space group is from materials knowledge of the family. The chunk file offers no reference entry at all for this chemistry, so it is uncorroborated and should be checked at v4 review.

formula_archetype: ACu5Q3 (A = K, Rb, Cs; Q = S, Se)

discriminate_from.bacu2s2_layered: the other ternary A-Cu-chalcogenide entry. It sits at ACu2X2 with a divalent alkaline-earth cation; here the cation is a large monovalent alkali and the anionic framework is far more copper-rich, which changes both the charge balance and the Cu coordination
discriminate_from.cu2se_superionic: adjacent chemistry, and copper mobility matters in both, but Cu2Se is a binary whose high-temperature phase is a cubic superionic conductor. Here the copper is held in a framework templated by the caesium and the compound is measured as an ordinary semiconductor
discriminate_from.argyrodite: the other copper and silver chalcogenide family valued for mobile cations and very low lattice thermal conductivity, but argyrodites are cubic and built around a halide or pnictide centre

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 024 for the Cs-Cu-Se host: all five compositions are alpha-CsCu5Se3 or its Sb-substituted variants, from the paper announcing alpha-CsCu5Se3 as a low-cost bulk selenide thermoelectric. The taxonomy has no entry for an alkali copper chalcogenide at this stoichiometry.

The space group and the layered description come from materials knowledge of the alpha form and are NOT corroborated by the chunk reference block, which returns the neighbouring compositions Cs3(Cu4Se3)2 C2/m mp-1188128, Cs2Cu5Se4 Cmcm mp-28467 and CsCuSe4 P2_12_12_1 mp-17095 -- none of them CsCu5Se3. Treat Cmcm as provisional and settle it from the paper at v4 review.
The alpha prefix is kept because the paper names the phase that way, which implies a second modification of the same compound; only the alpha structure is assigned.

formula_archetype: Cu4Sn7X16 (X = S, with the Se-substituted solid solution included)

discriminate_from.cu2gese3: the entry the rest of the Cu-S-Se-Sn host takes. Cu2SnSe3 is a monoclinic diamond-like framework with tin in tetrahedral coordination; here tin is octahedral in SnS6 sheets and the copper sits between them, which is different coordination chemistry at a different stoichiometry
discriminate_from.cdi2_1t: the SnS2 sheet motif on its own. The sheets are the same building block, but the interlayer here is filled by copper and additional tin, so there is no van der Waals gap and no dichalcogenide stoichiometry
discriminate_from.stannite_kesterite: the other Cu-Sn-S structure a composition like this could be swept into, tetragonal and fully tetrahedral at Cu2(Fe,Zn)SnS4; it shares no coordination motif with an octahedral tin sulfide

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 024 for one composition in the Cu-S-Se-Sn host, Cu4Sn7.5S14Se2, whose paper is on the improved thermoelectric performance of solid solution Cu4Sn7.5S16. It is a real line compound with a name, not a parse artefact, so parking it in unresolved_crystalline would lose information -- but it is also not the Cu2SnSe3 the other four compositions are.

The rhombohedral setting is from materials knowledge and is provisional: the chunk file gives no reference entry for this formula. R-3m rather than R-3 in particular is not settled here, and the structure is sometimes described as a defect or vacancy-ordered variant rather than as a simple layered stacking.
Entered as layered van der Waals to match cdi2_1t, which is the sheet it is built from, with the caveat that copper in the interlayer means the gap is filled rather than open.

display_name: Molten inorganic salt (ionic melt above the melting point)
formula_archetype: an ionic salt measured entirely above its melting point
representative_materials: molten nitrate and carbonate heat-transfer salts

discriminate_from.liquid_metal: the existing entry for a melt, but it is written for liquid metals and molten alloys, with a Ga-Zn melt as its exemplar and electronic conduction assumed. A molten nitrate conducts by ion migration and has a completely different transport signature, so filing it here would assert the wrong mechanism
discriminate_from.amorphous: a solid that lacks long-range order at the measurement temperature. A melt is not a frozen glass; it is above its melting point, and the reported quantity is a liquid thermal conductivity
discriminate_from.perovskite: not related, and listed only as a trap: KNO3 in its solid form is an aragonite-type or calcite-like oxide salt and could be swept into an oxide entry by anyone who did not check the measurement temperature against the melting point

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 025 for the K-N-O host. Its five samples come from a paper on thermal conductivity measurement of molten salts by the transient hot-wire method, and the measured window is 611-679 K. KNO3 melts at about 607 K, so every point in this host is taken on the liquid. Assigning any crystalline prototype would attach a structure the samples do not have at the temperature they were measured.

The solid sequence is recorded here for reference rather than assigned: aragonite-type orthorhombic Pmcn phase II below about 401 K, then calcite-like trigonal R-3m phase I up to the melt. Neither is inside the measured window.

No mp_id belongs on this entry, because Materials Project describes periodic crystals and a melt has no periodic structure. The chunk reference block does return KNO3 Pnma (62) mp-5158 at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references; that is a correct description of the ambient solid and simply not the phase measured.
Kept deliberately separate from liquid_metal rather than widening that entry, so that ionic and electronic melts stay distinguishable at v4 review.

formula_archetype: A2Ti2Pn2O (A = Na, Ba; Pn = As, Sb)

discriminate_from.bi2o2se_layered: the other layered oxide-pnictide-like entry, but its fluorite-type Bi2O2 slab puts oxygen in the cation-rich block and the chalcogen in a separate square net. Here the oxygen sits at the centre of a Ti4 square, giving anti-CuO2 Ti2O sheets, and the antimony caps them. The oxygen and the pnictogen are in the same slab, not in alternating ones
discriminate_from.zrcusias_1111: the 1111 oxypnictide, where a fluorite-type RE2O2 layer alternates with an antifluorite-type pnictide layer. That is a genuinely two-block structure with P4/nmm symmetry; the Na2Ti2Sb2O block is a single Ti2OSb2 slab in I4/mmm with alkali metal between
discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: shares the I4/mmm body-centred stacking of an A cation between anionic slabs, and Na2Ti2Sb2O is sometimes described as a filled 122 variant. It is not one: the 122 slab is a pure TX4 tetrahedral network with no interstitial anion, and removing the oxygen here changes the titanium oxidation state and the electronic structure entirely
discriminate_from.ruddlesden_popper: the other structure built from a square oxide sheet with a rocksalt-like interlayer. The Ti2O sheet here is an anti-structure -- oxygen at the square centre, metal at the corners -- which is the reverse of the perovskite TiO2 sheet in an RP phase

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 025 for the Na-O-Sb-Ti host, whose single composition Na2Ti2Sb2O has 5 samples from a paper on the physical properties of the layered pnictide oxides Na2Ti2Pn2O with Pn = As and Sb. The taxonomy has entries for the fluorite-block oxide pnictides (bi2o2se_layered, zrcusias_1111) but none for the anti-CuO2 Ti2O sheet family, which is a distinct electronic system: the titanium square lattice with a central oxygen gives a d1 sheet that shows a density-wave anomaly rather than a band gap.

The reference block supports the structure strongly and independently: Na2Ti2Sb2O I4/mmm (139) mp-6328 at hull 0.000 with 20 ICSD references, which is by far the best-attested entry in this chunk. mp-6328 is recorded in structure_database_candidates language here only as a note; per project convention the mp_id field in the seed taxonomy stays null and is resolved in stage 2.

BaTi2Sb2O and BaTi2As2O are included as representative materials because they are the superconducting members of the same structural family and would otherwise be candidates for a separate one-off entry.

formula_archetype: MX2O8 (M = Zr, Hf; X = W, Mo)
typical_space_group: P2_13 (198) alpha, Pa-3 (205) beta above about 430 K

discriminate_from.reo3_wo3: the corner-sharing octahedral framework this is often compared to. ZrW2O8 is not built of octahedra alone: half its polyhedra are WO4 tetrahedra, and crucially each tetrahedron has one terminal, singly coordinated oxygen. That free corner is what allows the transverse vibration responsible for the negative thermal expansion, and a ReO3 framework has no such corner
discriminate_from.pyrochlore: the other cubic A2B2O7 framework of corner-linked polyhedra, and a natural confusion because ZrV2O7 and ZrW2O8 sit near it in composition. Pyrochlore is fully octahedral with an interpenetrating A2O network; here the zirconium is octahedral but the tungsten is tetrahedral and there is no second network
discriminate_from.garnet: cubic, and also mixes octahedral and tetrahedral cation sites, but it is a dense fully corner- and edge-shared silicate-type framework with no terminal oxygen and positive thermal expansion
discriminate_from.fluorite_oxide: where an MO2 stoichiometry would otherwise route a zirconium-tungsten oxide. ZrW2O8 is not a defect fluorite; it is an open framework with roughly a third of the volume unoccupied, which is why it is a poor thermal conductor

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 025 for the O-W-Zr host, whose five samples all sit at ZrW2O8 and whose paper is on the unusual thermal conductivity of the negative thermal expansion material. This is a well-defined structure type with a large literature, not a parse artefact or an unresolved composition, so parking it in unresolved_crystalline would lose real information.

The reference block gives Zr(WO4)2 P2_13 (198) mp-18778 with 7 ICSD references, the strongest evidence for any structure in this host and in agreement with the assignment. Its hull value of 0.074 is expected rather than alarming: ZrW2O8 is metastable with respect to the binary oxides at all temperatures below about 1380 K and is recovered by quenching, so e_above_hull cannot be read as a stability argument here.

The alpha to beta transition at about 430 K is an order-disorder transition of the WO4 tetrahedral orientations, P2_13 to Pa-3. It does not change the prototype and both settings belong to this entry. The O-W-Zr measured window of 10-386 K stays below it, so no host in this chunk crosses it.
The other two reference entries for this host, Zr9W4O3 at hull 0.588 and ZrW2O11 at hull 0.439, are computed-only phases and neither is a candidate.

formula_archetype: elemental group 15, puckered honeycomb layers
typical_space_group: Cmce (64), also set as Bmab or Cmca

discriminate_from.a7_rhombohedral: the other layered elemental pnictogen structure and the entry this would otherwise be forced into. A7 is the grey arsenic type, rhombohedral R-3m, and for phosphorus it is the high-pressure form reached above about 5 GPa. A17 is orthorhombic Cmce, is the ambient stable allotrope, and has a band gap of about 0.3 eV where A7 phosphorus is semimetallic. The reference block separates them cleanly: P Cmce mp-157 with 25 ICSD references against P R-3m mp-130 with 4
discriminate_from.graphite_layered: the archetype for a van der Waals stack of honeycomb sheets. The phosphorus sheet is puckered rather than flat because each atom is three-coordinate with a lone pair, which is what makes the in-plane transport strongly anisotropic between the armchair and zigzag directions rather than isotropic
discriminate_from.trigonal_te: the other elemental chain or layer semiconductor with strong anisotropy, but tellurium is built from helical covalent chains in P3_121, not from layers

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 025 for the P host, where two of the three papers are on the thermoelectric power of bulk black phosphorus and on large anisotropic thermal transport in bulk single crystals. The anisotropy is the point of both measurements, so assigning the isotropic-looking a7_rhombohedral entry would misdescribe exactly what is reported.

The reference block is decisive and ICSD-backed: P Cmce (64) mp-157 carries 25 ICSD references against 5 for the simple cubic Pm-3m form, 4 for R-3m and 2 for P-1, all of which are high-pressure phases. The hull value of 0.030 for mp-157 against 0.000 for the triclinic entry is a DFT artefact of van der Waals treatment, not a statement that black phosphorus is metastable.

White and red phosphorus are deliberately not covered. White is molecular P4 and red is an amorphous or polymeric network; neither is this layered crystal, and a sample of either should go to amorphous or to a molecular entry instead.
Set as Cmce because that is the current symbol; older literature and some database entries use Cmca or Bmab for the same group, which is a labelling difference and not a different structure.

formula_archetype: FePb4Sb6S14

discriminate_from.stibnite: the parent Sb2S3 ribbon structure, and the closest relative. Jamesonite is built from comparable SbS3 pyramidal ribbons but they are cross-linked by lead in irregular seven- and eight-fold sites and by iron in a distinct octahedral site, which changes both the stoichiometry and the chain topology. Sb2S3 has no cation other than antimony
discriminate_from.tetrahedrite: the other earth-abundant copper or lead antimony sulfide family reached from this chemistry. Tetrahedrite is a cubic I-43m framework at Cu12Sb4S13 built on tetrahedral copper; jamesonite is monoclinic and has no tetrahedral transition-metal site of that kind
discriminate_from.bi_chalcogenide_complex: the entry that absorbs complicated bismuth chalcogenides whose structures are each their own. Jamesonite is not in that situation -- it is a single named mineral structure with a settled description -- so it earns an entry rather than a catch-all
discriminate_from.unresolved_crystalline: where this composition would otherwise land, and the reason for proposing: FePb4Sb6S14 is a mineral with a name and a known structure, and parking it as unresolved would discard that

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 025 for the Pb-S-Sb host, where three of the five samples are FePb4Sb6S14 or its Sn-substituted variants and one paper is explicitly on high-performance thermoelectrics from earth-abundant materials in this chemistry.

Neither reference block returns jamesonite itself. TEDesignLab gives Sb6Pb4S13 P1 (1) mp-27907, which is the same cation ratio at one sulfur less and with no iron, and Materials Project returns the iron-free lead antimony sulfosalts Sb8(PbS5)3, Sb8Pb7S19 and Sb4Pb5S11 plus a manganese analogue MnSb6(Pb2S7)2. The manganese entry is the informative one: it is the same structural family with Mn in the place of Fe, which corroborates the octahedral divalent-cation site without naming the iron member. The space group is from materials knowledge, not from these entries, and should be checked at v4 review.

The iron in FePb4Sb6S14 is a full stoichiometric site, not a dopant, even though it falls below the 5 at.% host cut because the formula has 25 atoms. The role vocabulary has no term for a stoichiometric constituent pushed below the threshold by formula size; this is worth raising separately.

Deliberately scoped to jamesonite rather than opened up to lead antimony sulfosalts in general. Boulangerite, zinkenite and semseyite are distinct structures, and a single broad entry would hide differences the reference block already shows.

display_name: Ag6Ge10P12 cubic silver germanium phosphide framework
formula_archetype: A6M10X12 (A = Ag, M = Ge, X = P)

discriminate_from.sphalerite: the simple binary tetrahedral parent. Ag6Ge10P12 is not a sphalerite superstructure: the silver does not sit on a tetrahedral cation site continuous with the germanium phosphide network, and the cell is body-centred with 28 atoms per formula unit rather than a two-atom basis
discriminate_from.defect_chalcopyrite_ovc: the other place an unusual cation count could be filed. Ordered vacancy compounds such as HgAl2Se4 keep the tetrahedral cation lattice of zincblende and empty one site in three in an ordered way; the cation to anion ratio here is not a vacancy-ordered derivative of a 1:1 tetrahedral lattice
discriminate_from.argyrodite: the closest competitor by composition, and the other silver-rich framework reached from Ag-M-X chemistry. Argyrodites such as Ag8GeSe6 are superionic, with silver mobile over many partially occupied sites; Ag6Ge10P12 is a fixed framework phosphide and is not an ionic conductor
discriminate_from.clathrate_i: also a covalent framework enclosing guests, but built from face-sharing cages of a single framework element with the guest rattling inside. The silver here is a framework constituent, not a cage guest

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 026 for the Ag-Ge-P host: all four samples are Ag6Ge10P12 within a small phosphorus excess and the single paper is on the origin of high thermoelectric performance in this earth-abundant phosphide.

Materials Project returns Ag3Ge5P6 I-43m (217) mp-17862 at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference, the same compound written at half the formula unit; that is where the space group comes from. mp_id is left null, as everywhere in the seed taxonomy, and is resolved in stage 2.

The framework description - linked germanium and phosphorus tetrahedral units enclosing the silver - is the part of this entry least fixed by the reference line and should be checked against the structure literature at v4 review. The formula and the space group are not in doubt.

Filed as tetrahedral diamond-like rather than as a cage compound because the silver is bonded into the framework rather than rattling in a cage, even though the transport signature - a semiconductor with low lattice thermal conductivity in a cubic cell - is the sort of thing that usually comes from a cage.

formula_archetype: AM3Q2 (A = alkali, M = Ag or Cu, Q = S or Se)

discriminate_from.ag2se_naumannite: the parent this compound was built to escape, and the entry it would otherwise be filed under. Ag2Se is a three-dimensional framework that goes superionic through an order-disorder transition near 400 K; inserting potassium cuts the silver selenide into anionic layers and suppresses that transition, which is the whole claim of the paper. Same chemistry, opposite structural behaviour
discriminate_from.bacu2s2_layered: the other layered coinage-metal chalcogenide entry, at AM2Q2 with a different slab connectivity rather than AM3Q2
discriminate_from.argyrodite: the other route silver chalcogenides take to low lattice thermal conductivity, through silver mobile over partially occupied sites in a three-dimensional framework rather than through reduced dimensionality
discriminate_from.cucrs2_layered: also an alkali or coinage metal between chalcogenide slabs, but there the slab is a transition-metal sulfide of edge-sharing octahedra and the copper is the interlayer species; here the slab is the silver selenide itself

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 026 for the Ag-K-Se host: all four samples are KAg3Se2 and the paper is titled Ag2Se to KAg3Se2: Suppressing Order-Disorder Transitions via Reduced Dimensionality.

TEDesignLab gives KAg3Se2 C2/m (12) mp-9782 at hull 0.000 as primary on one ICSD reference. Its other entries, KAgSe P4/nmm mp-16236 and K2Ag4Se3 C2/m, are neighbouring phases of the same ternary rather than polymorphs of this compound.

The type is named after the compound itself rather than after KCu3S2 because the isotypy with the copper sulfide is from materials knowledge and was not checked against a structure database. If it holds, rename the entry at v4 review and keep KCu3S2 as the type.
Structural class is recorded as layered van der Waals for want of a closer label in the declared vocabulary; the interlayer bonding is ionic, through the potassium cations, not van der Waals.

formula_archetype: A2B2O6, usually written ABO3

discriminate_from.pyrochlore: the full A2B2O7 parent and the entry this would otherwise be filed under. The corner-sharing B2O6 octahedral network is identical. What is missing is the O-prime anion on the 8b site, which in the full pyrochlore builds the interpenetrating A2O-prime sublattice; the A site itself stays fully occupied, so the formula reads A2B2O6 rather than A2B2O7
discriminate_from.ksbo3_bi3ru3o11: the other cubic ABO3 antimonate framework and the real competitor for a formula such as AgSbO3 or NaSbO3. The KSbO3 type is built from edge-sharing Sb2O10 octahedral dimers linked at their corners in Pn-3; this is the ordinary corner-sharing pyrochlore network in Fd-3m with a cell near 10.2 A. The same composition can take either, so they have to be separated by cell and space group rather than by formula
discriminate_from.perovskite: the third structure open to an ABO3 oxide, and what this is not: no twelve-coordinate A site and no single corner-sharing octahedral network of the perovskite kind
discriminate_from.hollandite: also an oxide framework built to hold loosely bound cations, but from edge-sharing double octahedral chains enclosing one-dimensional tunnels rather than a three-dimensional pyrochlore network

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 026 for the Ag-O-Sb host, where all four samples are AgSbO3 and the first paper is titled Thermoelectric properties of AgSbO3 with defect pyrochlore structure - the structure is named in the source rather than inferred from the formula.

The taxonomy already had pyrochlore at A2B2O7, and chunk 022 proposed beta_pyrochlore_ab2o6 for the case where half the A cations are missing. This is a third member of the family and a different defect: A full, O-prime empty. Keeping the three separate follows the same logic that keeps filled and unfilled skutterudite apart.

Materials Project does not hold the phase in usable form. It ranks Ag3SbO4 P4_122 mp-1202934 first on one ICSD reference, carries AgSbO3 only as a computed monoclinic C2 (5) structure mp-860791 at hull 0.044, and its one Fd-3m entry mp-1214924 is written AgSbO12 at hull 1.047. mp_id is left null.

The vacant O-prime site leaves the A cation weakly bound in an oversized cage, which is the standard explanation for the low lattice thermal conductivity of these oxides. AgSbO3 is studied as a transparent conductor and a photocatalyst as well as a thermoelectric, always with this same structural description.

formula_archetype: MX (M = Si or Ge, X = P or As)

discriminate_from.layered_ges: the entry GeAs would otherwise be forced into, and the closest relative. GeS and GeSe are orthorhombic Pnma with puckered double layers and no metal-metal bonding; GeAs is monoclinic C2/m and every slab contains Ge-Ge dimers, which is what a pnictogen anion rather than a chalcogen one requires for charge balance
discriminate_from.mos2_2h: a layered van der Waals semiconductor with the same stacking idea, but trigonal prismatic MX2 slabs at a different stoichiometry
discriminate_from.cdi2_1t: the octahedral 1T layered arrangement, again at MX2 rather than MX
discriminate_from.sphalerite: the three-dimensional tetrahedral alternative for a 1:1 compound of these groups. GeAs is not isotropic, and the anisotropy is the point of the paper that measures it
